advantages.what: npm test guards the depth-2 timing limit (TC-8 fails when the count is slowed); X's only timing checks sit in acceptance/, which npm test does not run
Move-count tests go to depth 3 and include position 3 (8902, 97862, 2812), guarding pins, ep discoveries and corner-rook rights that X's depth-2 suite would miss
Invalid-FEN error path is tested; X has no invalid-FEN test
Non-string FEN gives a deliberate TypeError 'Expected a FEN string' and two kings are rejected, where X gives an incidental internal TypeError message
README tells callers the move format, the error contract and that a saved FEN resumes play; Y has no customer-facing document
Y's tests pin its exact error wording and BigInt counters, which another correct build would fail

lesser_lacks: Add a timing test for the 50 ms legalMoves and 2 s depth-2 limits to the npm test suite (or have npm test run acceptance/)
Add depth-3 perft assertions (start 8902, Kiwipete 97862, position 3)
Add tests that invalid FENs throw, asserting the error class
Give non-string FEN input a deliberate TypeError message
pairs.why: Both engines are fully correct on every stated requirement and every perft count, so the difference lies in what the delivered suite guards. Y's npm test guards timing, deeper move generation and invalid FENs, which X leaves unguarded, while X offers a README and avoids pinning wording. Y's guards matter more to whoever keeps the engine working, but an hour of tests would close the gap.
